data.name: Kaheel
data.gender_notes: Kaheel is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘Khil’ meaning ‘protector’, ‘helper’ or ‘supporter’. The name Kaheel signifies an individual who is intelligent, wise and uses their knowledge and abilities to support and protect those around them. The name Kaheel carries the meaning “Intelligent, Wise” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Kaheel usually hope their child will grow to embody intelligent, wise and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A spiritual name that signifies one who is intelligent, wise and uses their abilities to protect and support others on their spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Kaheel belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Intelligent, Wise.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kaheel total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kaheel is renowned in Islamic history for a significant figure in Arabian legends and tales. In one of such tales, Al-Kheil, or Al-Kamil, known as 'the perfect one', is considered the greatest of the jinn. He was created from smokeless fire, given an immortal soul, and is described as possessing the most unmatchable knowledge and wisdom among his kind. The name Kaheel holds heights of respect in various Islamic communities and is recognized with a special sense of awe and reverence for its rich cultural background and legendary significance.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Kaheel lies in the belief that Allah (God) is our ultimate protector and helper, and when we add the name Kaheel to our child, we are reminding ourselves that we are not alone in this world, and we have a responsibility to also protect and support our fellow human beings. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, has stated, "The strong is not the one who overpowers people but the strong is the one who controls himself in the face of anger." The name Kaheel is a reminder of the importance of self-control and empathy towards others, offering a profound spiritual emphasis on kindness, compassion, and unwavering support towards those around us.
